newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Leonische Drahtwerke opens Slovak plant.
newsitem.headline: Leonische Drahtwerke opens Slovak plant.

text.p: German cable producer Leonische Drahtwerke AG Nuremberg on Thursday opened its third production plant in Slovakia.
The new plant, which cost eight million marks, was opened by Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik, who said the new factory highlighted Slovakia as a favourable production base.
Leoni Slowakia s.r.o. is wholly-owned by Leonische Drahtwerke, which has invested some 25 million marks into its three Slovak factories, employing some 1,600 Slovak workers, most of them women.
Leoni Slowakia managers said this year's production volume was estimated at 1.4 billion crowns, compared to some 800 million crowns in 1995.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG is Germany's biggest investor in Slovakia having invested 215 million marks since 1991 in its car assmebly plant in Bratislava.
